# Content Lessons — demo-mira

This file starts small and grows. After each piece, the Lessons Loop (`engine/4-lessons-loop.md`)
diffs the machine's final draft against the published version, extracts generalizable rules, and
— only on the author's explicit yes — appends them here.

**Lessons override `voice-guide.md` and `style-guide.md` when they conflict.** They are the
author's own confirmed edits, which outrank any general rule.

## File precedence in this pack
1. `content-lessons.md` (this file) — distilled from shipped work; wins every conflict.
2. `voice-guide.md` — the register authority and the DNA.
3. `style-guide.md` — who the persona is, what she writes, who reads it.

## Seed lessons (invented with the persona — the starting taste)
- Name the object before naming its function. "The board" first; what it scheduled second. A
  reader who can see the thing will follow the argument about it.
- One scene per idea. If a paragraph needs two rooms, it is two paragraphs.
- Quote a person's exact wording, including the part that is not tidy. The hesitation is the
  evidence that a human said it.
- The verdict appears once, late, in plain words. If it needs restating, the scenes did not do
  their work.
- Never end on a summary. End on something a person said, or something still in the building.

## Learned lessons (demo entries — what the loop appends in a live instance)
<!-- Each entry: date · the change observed in the published version · the generalizable rule. -->
- 2026-07-11 · Author cut a paragraph explaining what a vehicle rotation is and instead let a
  scheduler say "two boats, three crews, one that's always in the yard." **Rule:** when a
  technical explanation and a person's sentence can both do the work, keep the sentence and cut
  the explanation.
- 2026-07-28 · Author changed "the cutover was difficult for the team" to "for eleven days
  somebody stayed until the last sailing." **Rule:** replace any sentence describing how people
  felt with the thing they did that showed it.
- 2026-08-14 · Author removed an em dash in eleven places and split the sentences instead.
  **Rule:** if a sentence needs an em dash to hold two thoughts, it is two sentences.
- 2026-09-02 · Author restored a detail the machine had dropped as incidental — the magnets were
  warm from the window. **Rule:** sensory detail that a witness volunteered is never incidental;
  it is the part that proves she was there. Restore it before trimming anything else.
- 2026-09-02 · Author refused a closing line the machine wrote ("Some things are worth keeping
  even when they stop being useful.") and ended on the brass rail instead. **Rule:** if the last
  line could be said about any object in any workplace, it is not the last line.
